title: Conditional Contributions
description: Distinguish conditional from unconditional contributions and determine when contribution revenue is recognized.
html:
What Is a Conditional Contribution?

A contribution is conditional when the agreement includes both:

  • A barrier that the recipient must overcome.
  • A right of return of transferred assets or a right of release from the donor's obligation.
BARRIER + RIGHT OF RETURN OR RIGHT OF RELEASE = CONDITIONAL CONTRIBUTION

Why Conditions Matter

A conditional contribution is generally not recognized as contribution revenue until the barrier has been substantially overcome.

BARRIER NOT YET SUBSTANTIALLY OVERCOME → NO CONTRIBUTION REVENUE YET BARRIER SUBSTANTIALLY OVERCOME → RECOGNIZE CONTRIBUTION

Example — Performance Barrier

Example

A foundation promises an NFP $300,000 if the organization successfully provides job training to 500 participants.

The agreement also states that the foundation is released from its promise if the required number of participants is not served.

The requirement to serve 500 participants represents a measurable performance barrier.

The donor also has a right of release.

PERFORMANCE BARRIER + RIGHT OF RELEASE → CONDITIONAL

Cash Received Before Condition Is Met

Sometimes the donor transfers cash before the recipient has satisfied the condition.

If the contribution remains conditional, the recipient generally does not immediately recognize contribution revenue.

Example

An NFP receives $120,000 in advance under a conditional grant.

The agreement requires the NFP to achieve a specified measurable outcome, and the donor can require repayment if the condition is not met.

CASH RECEIVED $120,000 CONDITION NOT YET MET → LIABILITY $120,000 NOT CONTRIBUTION REVENUE

When the Condition Is Met

Once the qualifying barrier has been substantially overcome, the contribution can generally be recognized.

BARRIER SUBSTANTIALLY OVERCOME → LIABILITY ↓ CONTRIBUTION REVENUE ↑

Condition vs. Restriction

This distinction is one of the most important concepts in NFP contribution accounting.

Condition Affects Whether Revenue Is Recognized Yet
Restriction Affects How Recognized Resources May Be Used

Restriction Example

A donor gives an NFP $75,000 and requires the money to be used for scholarships.

Assume there is no barrier that must be overcome and no right of return.

PURPOSE RESTRICTION BUT NO CONDITION → RECOGNIZE CONTRIBUTION WITH DONOR RESTRICTIONS

Condition Example

A donor promises $75,000 only if the NFP successfully enrolls 200 students in a specified program.

The donor is released from the promise if the target is not achieved.

BARRIER + RIGHT OF RELEASE → WAIT TO RECOGNIZE

Some Indicators of a Barrier

A barrier may involve requirements such as:

  • Achieving a measurable outcome.
  • Achieving a specified level of service.
  • Meeting a matching requirement.
  • Incurring qualifying expenditures.
  • Following specific requirements that are related to the purpose of the agreement.

Matching Requirement Example

Example

A donor promises to contribute $100,000 if the NFP first raises $100,000 from other donors.

The donor is released from the promise if the matching requirement is not met.

MATCHING REQUIREMENT + RIGHT OF RELEASE → CONDITIONAL CONTRIBUTION

Administrative Requirements

Not every requirement automatically creates a substantive barrier.

Routine administrative or reporting requirements alone may not be enough to make an otherwise unconditional contribution conditional.

Conditional AND Restricted

A contribution can contain both a condition and a donor restriction.

Example

A donor promises $200,000 if an NFP serves 1,000 families.

Once earned, the money must be used specifically for food assistance.

FIRST: SATISFY CONDITION ↓ RECOGNIZE CONTRIBUTION THEN: APPLY DONOR RESTRICTION ↓ WITH DONOR RESTRICTIONS

CPA Decision Process

ASK #1 IS THERE A BARRIER? ASK #2 IS THERE A RIGHT OF RETURN OR RELEASE? IF BOTH EXIST: CONDITIONAL ↓ WAIT UNTIL BARRIER IS SUBSTANTIALLY OVERCOME ↓ THEN DETERMINE DONOR RESTRICTION

Key Takeaways

  • Conditional contributions generally contain a barrier and a right of return or release.
  • Contribution revenue generally waits until the barrier is substantially overcome.
  • Cash received before a condition is met may generally be reported as a liability.
  • A donor restriction is different from a donor condition.
  • A contribution may be both conditional and donor-restricted.

quiz.prompt: A donor transfers $150,000 to an NFP. The NFP must first achieve a specified measurable performance target, and the agreement requires the money to be returned if the target is not achieved. The target has not yet been met. How should the NFP generally report the $150,000 received?

choices.text: A liability until the barrier is substantially overcome
An increase in permanently restricted equity

quiz.explanation: The measurable performance barrier together with the donor's right of return makes the contribution conditional. Because cash was received before the barrier was substantially overcome, the amount is generally reported as a liability rather than contribution revenue.
